aggregation: Useful burst work sums successful critical requests completed within 100 ms of schedule over three bursts in each run; charts show medians with observed min/max, not confidence intervals. Burst p95 is the median of each run's worst-burst successful p95. Table rates/p95 are medians; rejection/deadline percentages pool counts. Background outcomes retained. SQL wait covers all services/priorities and divides total wait time by acquisitions that waited.
deadline_scope: The 20 ms client timeout with 80 ms SQL delay intentionally induces failures. Deadline errors remain a subset of transport_errors in raw output; other transport errors are zero. Queue cancellation counts a server-observed canceled waiting entry, not database-side termination.
body_scope: Known small bodies are buffered before waiting so net/http observes HTTP/1.1 disconnects. Large/unknown bodies stay streaming and fail-fast; proxy upload timeout is explicit. Queue bounds do not cover metadata/upload preparation.

criteria.interpretation: Median run-level outcomes for each deployment; useful work includes queue and scheduling delay. Short-burst improvement is tested separately from sustained overload. Caller-deadline failures are deliberately induced and shown, not silently removed.

limitations: Local short experiments, no durable queue, preemption, retries, distributed budget, production capacity or starvation guarantee. Aging changes scheduling preference, not hard priority reservations. Adaptive feedback excludes waiting; client useful-work measurement includes it.
